2 Maccabees — Instructions and Commands

Instructions · All Old Testament books · Original Torah and New Testament index

22 additional passage records · 32 quoted verse units. Read 2 Maccabees in Saints Translation.

This is a working instruction register organized by topic and then classification. Open a passage for its exact wording, source link and context note. Historical orders and rhetorical or poetic addresses retain their original setting; their presence here does not make them universal laws.

Review status: Working catalogue: the source collection covers every Old Testament book currently in Saints.Bible. Individual commands, repeated formulations, speakers and Christian application still require further review; this is not a certified exhaustive count of laws.

Topics: Faith, repentance and allegiance · Worship, prayer and holy things · Mercy, neighbors and the vulnerable · Family, marriage and household · Historical commissions, journeys and public life

Faith, repentance and allegiance

Historical · 4 passage records

2 Maccabees 7:16

Record type: Historical direction. Source section: The Fourth and Fifth Brothers.

2 Maccabees 7:16 — Looking at the king, he said, “Although mortal, you have authority among human beings and do what you will. But do not suppose our people have been abandoned by God.

Context and scope: A direction recorded in this narrative. Its original speaker, recipient and occasion must be retained; recording an order does not establish that God approves it or commands every believer to repeat it.

Historical — rejected · 2 passage records

2 Maccabees 6:1 – 2 Maccabees 6:6

Record type: Reported hostile or rejected order. Source section: The Temple Defiled and the Customs Forbidden.

2 Maccabees 6:1 — Not long afterward the king sent an elderly Athenian to compel the Jews to depart from their ancestral laws and cease conducting their lives according to God’s laws,

2 Maccabees 6:2 — and also to defile the temple in Jerusalem and name it for Olympian Zeus, and the one at Gerizim for Zeus the Protector of Strangers, in keeping with those who inhabited the place.

2 Maccabees 6:3 — The intensification of the evil was harsh and wholly grievous.

2 Maccabees 6:4 — For the temple was filled by the nations with debauchery and revels. They dallied with prostitutes, had intercourse with women in the sacred enclosures, and also brought inside things that were unfit.

2 Maccabees 6:5 — The altar was filled with forbidden things excluded by the laws.

2 Maccabees 6:6 — It was impossible to keep the Sabbath, observe ancestral festivals, or even profess simply to be a Jew.

Context and scope: This order is recorded as hostile, coercive or contrary to faithful obedience in its narrative context. It is not included as a divine command to obey.
